delete.description:
Takes a folder out of the library. Its files stay exactly where they are. Not while a
file in it is converting, or made and waiting for another app to let go of its original:
its result is about to take the original's place.

post.description: Starts scanning every library folder. Nothing in them changes.
Stops the scan after the file it's on; resuming carries on from there.

put.description:
Keeps the owner's choices. Turning the reports off takes them out of the anime folders at
once; turning them on writes them again. So with the pictures next to each show: off, the
ones Kura wrote go at once; on, Kura's care writes them now.

Checks the key with TMDB, then keeps it on this PC. What AniList alone matched is then
identified again, by TMDB's lists.

delete.description: Forgets the key. Titles Kura already looked up stay.

post.description:
Makes the changes the owner reviewed, journaled so History can undo them. None is made
when Kura proposes any of them differently now.

Deletes videos the way Kura deletes: into the quarantine on their own drive, with their
subtitles, journaled so History can put them back till the quarantine is cleared out.

get.description: Every tidy-up applied and every scan, newest first.

post.description:
Puts back what a tidy-up moved, or what couldn't go back last time. For a conversion,
the original comes back in the converted file's place.

get.description: Every video not at the standard yet, with what each way of converting it would take.

One side of the comparison: a frame of the file as it is (`before`), or as `way` makes
it (`after`), taken at one of three points (0, 1 or 2: 15%, 50% and 80% of the way in).

post.description: Puts files at the end of the queue, to convert now, at night, or after what waits.
Stops the file converting now (it starts over on resuming) and takes no other.

On a drive without room for all that waits on it, the files that fit convert, and the
rest wait for room while the others go. The queue goes on if it paused.

Deletes everything set aside on a drive now, however recently, to make room there: it
can't be put back after. Kura asks the owner first. Files waiting for room look again.

put.description: Converts whenever files wait, or only at night (23:00 to 07:00).

On the nights-only schedule: tonight's run stops taking files at 03:00, so Windows' sleep
comes back sooner, or goes on till 07:00.

post.description: Passes over a file: the one converting stops, one waiting leaves the line.

Marks a file whose conversion failed as broken: the library counts it among the files
that won't play, and it isn't converted again till it changes.

A failed or skipped file goes back in the queue, last; one made and waiting for another
app to let go of its original is tried again now ("Try now").
Puts a converted file's original back in its place, from quarantine.

get.description: How big each part of Kura's data is, and the quarantine on each drive.

post.description:
Moves Kura's data to another folder as the engine starts again: the app starts it again
right after asking.

Writes the export zip (the database, settings, file changes and a manifest) into a
folder, never over another file.
Makes a backup now, checked like the nightly ones (and kept apart from them).

Puts an export's records in place as the engine starts again, the way a backup is
restored: the app starts it again right after asking.
Restores a backup as the engine starts again: the app starts it again right after.

get.description: What Kura settled as it started again after closing unexpectedly, while it's news.

post.description: The owner has seen it: Home doesn't tell it again.

get.description:
Whether Kura's records are damaged, and what can bring them back; null while they're
fine.

post.description:
Restores the newest backup that opens over the damaged records, which are kept beside it
as they are. The app starts the engine again right after.

Sets the damaged records aside as they are, so Kura starts again with new ones, as on its
first day. The app starts the engine again right after.
